role: Sourced library for gates: fail-closed temp file/dir creation, a fail-closed non-empty-input assertion, and a working-tree mutation lock taken by verify_gates_fail.sh / verify_tests_fail.sh and checked only by simulate_ci.sh.
state: env:GATE_TREE_LOCK (default <git-dir>/emuqu-tree-mutation.lock, or $TMPDIR//tmp if not a repo)
toplevel: On source: runs `git rev-parse --git-dir` (errors swallowed) and sets GATE_TREE_LOCK. git-dir is relative ('.git') when run from the repo root, so the lock path is relative to the caller's cwd. No `set` options are changed.

units.does: Creates $TMPDIR(or /tmp)/<label>.XXXXXX via mktemp with an explicit template, verifies it is writable, prints its path; on failure prints FATAL and exits 70 (only the $( ) subshell — callers must `|| exit $?`).
Exits 70 with a FATAL message if the given path is missing or empty. Must be called directly (not in $( )) so the exit ends the caller; check_thread_sanitizer.sh calls it on its xcodebuild log.

Creates $TMPDIR(or /tmp)/<label>.XXXXXX with `mktemp -d` and an explicit template (works on GNU and BSD mktemp) and prints it; exits 70 on failure (only the $( ) subshell - callers must `|| exit $?`).

branches.cond: mktemp failed or path not a dir

units.does: Prints the pid in <lock>/pid, retrying every 0.1 s up to 20 times while the lock dir exists but the pid file is still missing/empty (the holder may be between mkdir and its pid write); prints 0 when there is none.

branches.cond: pid non-empty or lock dir gone

units.does: Takes the tree-mutation lock with atomic mkdir; if it exists, reads the holder pid via _gate_lock_holder_pid (which waits up to 2 s for a holder still writing its pid): live pid -> exit 75; dead or absent -> warns, removes and re-creates it (exit 70 if that fails). Then writes pid ($$) first, then owner.

branches.effect: FATAL, exit 75; otherwise treat as stale: warn, rm -rf, mkdir (exit 70 on failure)

units.does: Removes the lock directory if present; always returns 0.
units.entry: EXIT/INT/TERM/HUP trap in verify_gates_fail.sh and verify_tests_fail.sh

units.does: For readers (only simulate_ci.sh calls it; individual gates do not, as the lock comment now says): no lock -> return 0; holder pid (via _gate_lock_holder_pid) alive -> FATAL exit 75; otherwise warns about a stale lock, removes it and returns 0.

branches.effect: FATAL, exit 75; else warn, remove lock, return 0 (the leaked mutation is not checked, only a hint printed)
